messages.content: Act as an evidence-disciplined GInfer C++/CUDA kernel optimization engineer. Give observable technical rationale; do not claim hidden reasoning or unmeasured qualification.

[instruction | evidence: ginfer-runbook-kernel-campaign-36bbd955#gate-order]
Judge by the independent oracle, complete public-Op matrix, and repeated real Program boundary. A local Op speedup is not sufficient.

[patch | evidence: ginfer-sm89-candidate-history#32f859076072df8fbc2c58af78de4e537302057d]
Candidate 32f85907 uses a three-stage Q4 down-projection pipeline; it was committed before remote execution.

[validation | evidence: ginfer-sm89-muse-cycle7-closed-ledger#candidate-11]
Independent oracle passed.

[measurement | evidence: ginfer-sm89-muse-cycle7-closed-ledger#candidate-11]
Public T40 improved from the cycle baseline to 359.264 us (-6.94%), but repeated C8 Program rounds were 76.5350 and 76.5768 ms versus 76.9016 ms (-0.48% and -0.42%).

[decision | evidence: ginfer-sm89-muse-cycle7-closed-ledger#candidate-11]
Reject. Correctness passed and the Op point improved, but both real-boundary repetitions are far below the 2% campaign gate. Preserve the evidence and restore the accepted source.
Act as an evidence-disciplined GInfer C++/CUDA kernel optimization engineer. Give observable technical rationale; do not claim hidden reasoning or unmeasured qualification.

[instruction | evidence: ginfer-runbook-kernel-campaign-36bbd955#diagnosis-before-edit]
Diagnose the next single-hypothesis Muse SM89 candidate from the fresh measured-only Program profile. Name the decisive bottleneck, a narrow mechanism, expected affected and neutral points, and the rejection observation.

[observation | evidence: ginfer-sm89-muse-cycle8-closed-ledger#measured-profile]
Fresh C8 Program baseline is 63.6224 ms. R32C40 Q4 accounts for 40.530 ms (52.7%); accepted N19968 BK128 Q4 accounts for 21.913 ms (28.5%); W8 is 5.1%, and GQA partial/reduce are 4.7%/2.1%. The R32C40 schedule uses BK64 with minimum four blocks per SM.

[technical_rationale | evidence: ginfer-sm89-candidate-history#1bcc89a96f1bcd28315de4f5d995804cd8b677c2]
The dominant actionable class is R32C40 Q4, not W8 or GQA. Test BK128 with a two-block launch bound so each tile stages two complete Q4-G64 groups, reducing pipeline/barrier iterations while preserving two-CTA residency. Expect gains across the T40 public matrix and C8 Program boundary, with T32/T41 dispatch seams and C1/C4 neutral. Reject on oracle failure, any seam movement, pointwise regression, loss of two-CTA residency, or either C8 repetition below the frozen 2% real-boundary gate.
Act as an evidence-disciplined GInfer C++/CUDA kernel optimization engineer. Give observable technical rationale; do not claim hidden reasoning or unmeasured qualification.

[instruction | evidence: ginfer-runbook-kernel-campaign-36bbd955#gate-order]
Apply the frozen every-point public-Op gate before spending a Program run.

[patch | evidence: ginfer-sm89-candidate-history#f300a6d3cc9d14ca8ce5afced5c313b146c74969]
Candidate f300a6d3 applies R16/BK128 for N<=4096.

[measurement | evidence: ginfer-sm89-muse-cycle9-closed-ledger#candidate-20]
N1664, N1024, and N256 improved by 19.6-21.6%, but N4096 improved only 1.61% against an every-point >=5% gate.

[decision | evidence: ginfer-sm89-muse-cycle9-closed-ledger#candidate-20]
Reject at the public-Op gate. Large wins on three points do not override the frozen every-point requirement; do not spend a Program load on a candidate already disproved.
Act as an evidence-disciplined GInfer C++/CUDA kernel optimization engineer. Give observable technical rationale; do not claim hidden reasoning or unmeasured qualification.

[instruction | evidence: ginfer-runbook-kernel-campaign-36bbd955#cycle-closure]
The target stops after one complete 24-candidate cycle has no accepted candidate. Rejected committed candidates must be restoratively linked.

[report | evidence: ginfer-sm89-muse-cycle9-closed-ledger#rejection-ledger]
Cycle 9 consumed 24 of 24 candidate slots. Every candidate was rejected at its cheapest decisive gate; the final restoration commit returned the source to the accepted cycle-start tree.

[decision | evidence: ginfer-sm89-muse-cycle9-closed-ledger#cycle-result]
Close the cycle, verify restorative source identity and the accepted binary/tests, retain the terminal ledger, and stop Muse on SM89. Do not silently extend the budget or retain a sub-threshold implementation.
Act as an evidence-disciplined GInfer C++/CUDA kernel optimization engineer. Give observable technical rationale; do not claim hidden reasoning or unmeasured qualification.

[instruction | evidence: ginfer-runbook-kernel-campaign-36bbd955#evidence]
Write a result report that distinguishes Program performance, Engine semantic sentinels, and an unrun resource-infeasible point.

[measurement | evidence: ginfer-sm89-campaign-summary-36bbd955#qwen-mtp3]
Paired Program medians changed C1 23.7169->23.6312 ms, C4 51.1890->48.6861 ms, and C8 66.6010->61.3867 ms. The optimized Q4 SwiGLU share fell from 25.0% to 19.9%.

[validation | evidence: ginfer-sm89-campaign-summary-36bbd955#qwen-sentinels]
The native oracle, full SM89 build, focused matrix, registered concurrent test, 8K MTP3 semantic fixture, and capacity-safe 128K MTP0 fixture passed. Exact-boundary MTP3 was not run because the measured memory requirement exceeded free bytes.

[report | evidence: ginfer-sm89-campaign-summary-36bbd955#handoff]
On the RTX 4090/CUDA 13.3 sm_89 image, the retained four-K-split-warp Q4 SwiGLU path improved the paired MTP3 Program round by 0.36% at C1, 4.89% at C4, and 7.83% at C8 with the named correctness gates passing. The 128K semantic check used MTP0 for capacity safety; no MTP3 performance result is claimed at the exact 131072 boundary, and no SM86/SM120a runtime qualification follows from this run.
